 O R D E R
This criminal original petition is filed seeking quashment of the proceedings in respect of Na.Ka.No.R2/32154/2017(Charge Sheet No.03/2017) on the file of the first respondent.

2.The case of the prosecution is that the 2nd respondent, who is working as Food Safety Officer,
Vickramasingapuram, Tirunelveli District, taken the food sample of Sindhu Chicken 65-Mix Powder from first accused's industries.
It was sent for analysis and found that it is misbranded.
On the payment of due price, the sample was lifted as per the procedure.
Notice was issued to the manufacturer under section 62A of the Act and he received the same.
The sample was sent to the food analyst and he sent an analyst report on 09/02/2017 to the designated officer.
The copy of the report was sent to A1 and he was also requested to express his willingness to send the sample for further analysis by the central lab.
The report shows that it is misbranded.
It does not satisfy the requirement of regulation 2.2.25.2(A) of the Act.

After obtaining proper sanction, the prosecution w a s l a u n c h e d s t a t i n g t h a t t h e a c c u s e d p e r s o n s h a v e c o m m i t t e d t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.793 of 2019.
offences punishable under sections 52, 55, 58 and 51 of the Act.
3.Seeking quashment of the same, this petition came to be filed by the petitioner on the ground that the mandatory requirement of the proper procedure has not been followed.
There was a delay in the analysis.
4.Heard both sides.
5.The first contention raised on the part of the petitioner is that the mandatory requirement of the procedure for lifting the sample has not been followed by the second respondent herein.
Whether such a proper procedure has been followed or not, can not be a matter for consideration in this petition.
It is the matter for trial.
If there is any violation of the mandatory procedure, then only the petitioner can take advantage of the same.
This is too an earlier stage to take up the point.
So this point is not available to this petitioner.
6.The second contention of the petitioner is that the sample was lifted on 20/04/2017, but it was a n a l y s e d m u c h a f t e r t h e p e r i o d 1 4 d a y s .
T h e r e p o r t h a s b e e n r e c e i v e d o n https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.793 of 2019.
. Even after it was analysed on 26/04/2017, it was completed only on 03/05/2017.
The report was sent on 09/05/2017.
According to the petitioner, it is a statutory violation.

The reason for S.Saroja vs The State Represented By on 28 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102178765/
2 violation is that due to the administrative reason, they are not in a position to complete the analysis within the prescribed time.
It is seen that analysis was done on 24/06/2017 within the prescribed time.
But, it was completed only, on 03/08/2017.
So whether the reason mentioned by the respondent for food analyst is accepted or not is a matter for consideration by the trial court.
Therefore, the acceptance or otherwise of the reason assigned cannot be a matter for consideration by this court.
It requires proper evidence and reason.

The report shows that it is a misbranded one,
because of the violation of the regulation 2.2(5)2(a).
7.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would say that the method of taking sample is not proper, since only polythene bag was used for taking the sample, which is a violation.
For that purpose, he would rely upon the judgment of this court reported in State Vs. Isakki Muthu (1992 CriLJ 2884).
In that case, Rule 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration was under consideration.
The above said Rule says that samples must be taken in a clear dry polythene bag or jars or other available https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD)No.793 of 2019.
container.
In that case, polythene bag was used for taking samples.
That was argued as violation.
But it was held that poly bag can be considered as a container.
8.The respondent would further rely upon the food Rules 2011 ruling 2.41(7) provision.
According to him, if the sealed bag is taken as sample, further sealed in a separate container is not required.
So answered the point that has been raised by the petitioner.
So I am of the considered view that no ground worth considering is made out by the petitioner to quash the proceedings.
The proceedings must be taken to its logical conclusion.
9.In the result, this criminal original petition is dismissed.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
